Verify SHA-256 Checksum and Readability of a Chunk Checkpoint

Source: R/security.R
verify_checkpoint.Rd

Validates that a chunk .rds checkpoint exists, matches its recorded SHA-256 sidecar digest (and optional expected_sha256), and deserializes cleanly via readRDS(). Protects slurm_collect() against silent corruption or partial writes on shared HPC filesystems.

Usage

verify_checkpoint(result_path, expected_sha256 = NULL, require_sidecar = FALSE)

Arguments

result_path

Path to a chunk_XXXX.rds checkpoint file.

expected_sha256

Optional 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 string to verify against in addition to the .sha256 sidecar file (if present).

require_sidecar

Logical; if TRUE, fails when no .sha256 sidecar exists and expected_sha256 is NULL. Default FALSE (verifies whenever a sidecar or expected_sha256 is available).

Value

A named list with ok (logical), sha256 (actual SHA-256 hex), expected_sha256, reason (NA_character_ when valid), and object (the deserialized chunk object when valid, else NULL).

Examples

tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(list(chunk_id = 1L, results = list()), tmp)
writeLines(digest::digest(tmp, algo = "sha256", file = TRUE), paste0(tmp, ".sha256"))
verify_checkpoint(tmp)$ok
#> [1] TRUE
unlink(c(tmp, paste0(tmp, ".sha256")))
